description: Debate about dominance of permanent five members could reignite if major powers block Costa Rican frontrunner The race to become the next UN secretary general could reach a decisive moment on Friday when a UN security council vote is likely to reveal whether the Costa Rican frontrunner for the post would be blocked by the big powers. categories: Planning policy | Politics | Advertising | Media | Commercial property | Business | Real estate | England | UK news
description: Reasons to refuse planning permission are limited to ‘public safety’ and ‘amenity’, writes James Ward In response to your report ( Rip out ugly clutter to help revive UK high streets, says thinktank, 13 November ) perhaps we could start with the harbinger of high-street decline, the digital advertising screen. You know the ones, the pavement-blocking LED monoliths, with screens on both sides broadcasting six ads per minute to passersby. Even as shops have shuttered, numbers of such ad machines skyrocketed 256% between 2018 and 2025. The ads shown are invariably for global mega-corporations, further driving commerce online, and for unhealthy products such as junk food, alcohol, gambling and vapes (although the latter are to be banned from 1 June 2027). At nearly 3 metres tall and 1.24 metres wide, they contribute to pavement clutter and disrupt sightlines of historic town centres.

description: Americans are at a real point of decision – not election day, but this heady, uncertain moment after Until 2026, the most important midterm year of the last quarter-century was very probably 2010. Barack Obama famously called the elections a “shellacking” for the Democratic party and he was right. Thanks to a sluggish economic recovery from the Great Recession and backlash against the passage of the Affordable Care Act, Republicans took control of the House with a 63-seat gain – the largest House sweep since the 1940s – and won six seats in the Senate. But the 2010 midterms were significant well beyond those numbers. It was the first election shaped by the rise of the Tea Party and its blend of rightwing economic populism and xenophobia.
